title: A Orbit for the Machine
premise: Vesper Lockridge, a xenolinguist whose mind was rewired by a deep-space accident so thoroughly that she no longer dreams in human languages, tends a forgotten beacon at the edge of contested space. When she intercepts a distress call in Ashkari — a language extinct for two centuries, and one only her altered brain can parse — she discovers the war between the Concord and the Ashkari remnant fleets hinges on a message the dying transmitter has carried for two hundred years: proof that the Concord's founding atrocity was engineered by its own founders. Pursued by Concord intelligence and guided by the ragtag crew of the salvage ship Kettle's Mercy who become her found family, Vesper must choose whether to deliver the message, knowing it will shatter the peace that depends on the lie. She delivers it — not as a broadcast, but as testimony given voice by the last living Ashkari speaker — ending the war by forcing both sides to grieve together rather than fight.
about_author: Ines Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else answered. They write science fiction about people who keep watch at the edges of things, and live aboard a converted tugboat with an unreasonable number of dictionaries.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On the lonely station Perihelion Nine, Vesper maintains a beacon whose commissioning records have been scrubbed from every archive. Her days are ritual and silence; her dreams arrive in colors and pressure, never words. The beat is quiet isolation — competence as a form of hiding.

chapters.title: A Language That Should Be Dust
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A distress signal arrives in Ashkari, extinct since the Purge of 2147. Her rewired mind parses it effortlessly — and the content terrifies her: coordinates, a warning, and a name the Concord erased. Emotional beat: the thrill of recognition curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Salvage Rights
chapters.summary: Ravi Okafor, captain of the salvage ship Kettle's Mercy, POV. Answering Vesper's panicked request for transport, Ravi and her crew — engineer Toma, medic Junie, and the ship's half-sentient nav system — find a woman clutching a data core like a relic. Beat: wary hospitality, the first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: What the Accident Left
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, flashback-woven. En route to the relay hub, she explains the neural accident that rebuilt her language centers — and why the Concord classified her as equipment, not a person. The crew listens without flinching. Beat: being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Hub at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. At the crowded relay hub, Vesper decodes more of the message while Junie quietly acquires forged transit papers. They learn Concord intelligence flagged the signal too. Beat: the noose tightening beneath ordinary noise.

chapters.title: Officer Hale Asks Politely
chapters.summary: Concord intelligence officer Dara Hale's POV. Hale interviews Vesper under the guise of routine inquiry, offering protection, reinstatement, personhood — if she surrenders the core. Vesper refuses. Beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. The Kettle's Mercy burns hard for the outer systems with a Concord corvette on their tail; Toma strips the ship to outrun it. Beat: adrenaline, banter under pressure, the crew choosing Vesper without saying so.

chapters.title: The Remnant Fleet
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They reach the Ashkari remnant fleet — descendants of the Purge survivors, still fighting a two-century-old war. Vesper translates the core's first full passage aloud: the Purge was ordered by the Concord's own founders, to seize Ashkari jump technology. Beat: history cracking open.

chapters.title: Speaker of the Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Elder Sef-Adunai, last fluent Ashkari speaker, POV. She tests Vesper — not her grammar but her grief — asking why a human carries their dead language in her skull. Vesper answers honestly: she doesn't know what she is anymore either. Beat: mutual recognition across loss.

chapters.title: Proof Is Not Enough
chapters.summary: Ravi's POV. The remnant war council wants to broadcast the core immediately as justification for a final strike. Ravi argues a revelation dropped like a bomb will only restart the slaughter. Beat: the theme made argument — justice outside the law needs witnesses, not weapons.

chapters.title: Hale's Net
chapters.summary: Dara Hale's POV. Hale, ordered to retrieve or destroy the core, begins doubting her own archives when she finds the same scrubbed records Vesper did. She buys time from her superiors with lies. Beat: the antagonist developing a conscience.

chapters.title: The Message in Full
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Working with Sef-Adunai, Vesper finishes translating the dying transmitter's complete testimony — recorded by an Ashkari archivist who hid inside the beacon network itself. The beacon Vesper tended was the archive's shell. Beat: devastating purpose; her meaningless job was a vigil all along.

chapters.title: Concord Border, Closed
chapters.summary: Toma's POV. The crew plans delivery to the Concord Assembly via neutral station Meridian, but the border seals; Hale's superiors suspect her. The crew votes to go anyway, knowing it may be a one-way trip. Beat: found family formalized into commitment.

chapters.title: What Vesper Dreams
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In Ashkari meditation with Sef-Adunai, Vesper finally dreams in words — Ashkari words. She realizes her rewiring wasn't damage but inheritance: the archivist seeded the language into minds that touched his beacons. Beat: identity reframed; she is the message's vessel.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Meridian
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. A remnant faction, fearing peace more than defeat, sells their route to the Concord. Ambush at Meridian; Toma is gravely wounded covering the escape. Beat: cost, rage, and Junie holding the line medically while the plan bleeds out.

chapters.title: Hale Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Dara Hale's POV. Hale intercepts the crippled Kettle's Mercy — and instead of firing, comes aboard with her own evidence cache, offering testimony against her masters. Beat: the law's servant defecting to justice.

chapters.title: The Long Silence Before
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hiding in a comet-shroud drift, the crew waits for the Assembly session where the truth can be entered into record. Vesper rehearses the testimony in two tongues. Quiet chapter; fear and tenderness, wills written, jokes told badly. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Assembly of Liars
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The delivery attempt: Hale demands floor access as an officer; the remnant strike fleet launches simultaneously, giving the lie urgency. Vesper takes the floor as the Assembly tries to silence her. Beat: climax ignition.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She delivers the archivist's message — speaking Ashkari aloud, Sef-Adunai's voice joined remotely in answer, the dead tongue alive between them. Evidence cascades onto public feeds. The strike fleet holds at the line, waiting. Beat: the climax's peak — truth as act, not artifact.

chapters.title: What the War Was For
chapters.summary: Sef-Adunai's POV. The Assembly fractures; founder-descendant houses fall; ceasefire orders ripple outward as both fleets stand down to listen. Sef-Adunai mourns publicly, and millions mourn with her. Beat: grief shared instead of weaponized.

chapters.title: Personhood, Granted
chapters.summary: Ravi's POV. Aftermath: tribunals, resignations, and a ruling that reclassifies neural-altered humans as persons. Hale testifies; Toma heals; the Kettle's Mercy is offered honors it declines. Beat: justice institutionalized at last, but the family knows the real work was theirs.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Machine
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper returns to Perihelion Nine — now a memorial archive — and recommissions the beacon herself, broadcasting the Ashkari language openly so it can never again be lost. She dreams in three languages now. Final beat: the keeper becomes the keeper of something chosen, surrounded by visitors, no longer alone.
